paper.title: AI as a cognitive collaborator: Assimilation and accommodation in human–machine teaming for innovation

paper.one_line_finding: Among analyzed individual participants (90 with GPT-4, 92 without AI), the AI arm had higher expert-rated solution novelty (7.1 vs 5.8) and quality (7.3 vs 6.2) on 10-point scales (p. 6, Table 2; p. 5, Measures).

arms.name: Individual No AI
arms.description: Worked alone without GenAI during the 90-minute innovation task (PDF p. 5, Procedures). The paper does not describe a matched activity during AI-arm training. Analyzed N is the individual row in Table 2 (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Team No AI
arms.description: Worked in dyads without GenAI (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Table 2 (PDF p. 6) prints N = 95 without identifying people versus dyads; analyzed people and clusters remain unknown. A matched activity during AI-arm training is not described.

arms.name: Individual AI
arms.description: Worked alone with GPT-4 during the 90-minute innovation task after a 45-minute module on prompt engineering and hands-on GPT-4 interaction (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Analyzed N is the individual row in Table 2 (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Team AI
arms.description: Worked in dyads with GPT-4 after the same training module (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Table 2 (PDF p. 6) prints N = 94 without identifying people versus dyads; analyzed people and clusters remain unknown.

studies.task: Complete an open-ended organizational innovation challenge, such as proposing a novel digital product, redesigning customer service, or integrating sustainability into an existing offering.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Procedures, names hands-on GPT-4 interaction and training; PDF p. 7 provides participants’ prompt examples. The model release year and exact version are not printed.

PDF p. 5, Measures
sources.quote: quality, novelty, and feasibility using a 10-point Likert scale adapted from Dell’Acqua et al. (2025). Raters were blind to participant conditions and identity, and inter-rater reliability was acceptable (ICC2 = 0.51).

estimates.notes: Separate overlapping analysis of the same study, not an additional sample. The Results text on PDF p. 6 explicitly interprets the Quality GenAI coefficient as individuals using GenAI versus individuals without it. The same predictor and parallel model structure support the individual-arm mapping for the other outcomes, as in the screening form; exact reference coding remains unreported. These coefficients are not coded as a marginal contrast of pooled AI arms. Table 3 prints no analysis counts, so n_treatment, n_control, and n_total remain null; Table 2 counts are not assigned to this regression. The coefficient symbol β does not establish standardization: outcome_scale and paper_effect remain null. Rating aggregation, treatment of dyad observations, and the SE estimator are unspecified, so unit is null and se_basis is unclear. The Table 4 mediation-adjusted direct effects are excluded.

not_extracted.what: Positive emotional change and emotional-engagement effects
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported affect rather than an evaluation of produced output (PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2; PDF p. 10, Appendix A). Table 6 (PDF p. 8), H3–2, additionally reports an accommodation effect: β = 0.520, p < .001; this is a post-treatment strategy association on the same out-of-scope self-report.

not_extracted.what: Negative emotional change
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported frustration and anxiety, not creativity or diversity scored on output (PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2; PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

not_extracted.what: Perceived performance: self-rated relative standing and solution feasibility
not_extracted.reason: Appendix A (PDF p. 10) labels these supplementary self-report outcomes. They are distinct from the retained expert-rated feasibility outcome; no full-sample numerical arm contrasts are printed for these self-reports.

not_extracted.what: Technology acceptance: intention to reuse GenAI and confidence in AI collaboration
not_extracted.reason: Attitudes and intentions measured by post-task survey, outside output-scored outcomes. Appendix A, PDF p. 10; no numerical treatment contrasts are printed.

not_extracted.what: Assimilation/accommodation classification and cognitive-strategy measures
not_extracted.reason: Strategies are classified after treatment from surveys and qualitative evidence; they were not randomized AI configurations and are analyzed as mediators. PDF p. 5, Measures, and PDF p. 10, Appendix A.

not_extracted.what: Open-ended reflections, illustrative prompt histories, and debrief interviews
not_extracted.reason: Qualitative process evidence rather than quantitative full-sample contrasts on scored creative output. PDF p. 7, Illustrative cases, and PDF p. 10, Appendix A.

not_extracted.what: Solution quality: direct and indirect mediation effects
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analysis conditions on post-treatment accommodation; both the adjusted direct effect and indirect effect are excluded. PDF p. 7, Table 4 (columns: direct effect, indirect effect, percent mediated, bootstrapped 95 % CI): "Quality .28** .12* 30 % [.05, 0.21]". No total effect is computed by adding these coefficients.

not_extracted.what: Solution quality: moderated mediation by emotional engagement
not_extracted.reason: Interaction of post-treatment cognitive strategy with emotional engagement, rather than a full-sample randomized arm contrast. open_items: Assignment unit and dyad-formation sequence are not stated. Stratified randomization is explicit (PDF p. 5, Procedures), but the strata do not establish individual versus team allocation. assignment_unit and clusters_per_arm remain null; the paper provides no cluster counts or cluster-SE description.

The recruited total is 371, not an explicitly reported randomized or final analyzed count (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Counts at assignment, exclusions, attrition, and an unambiguous total analyzed headcount are missing.

Table 2 reports Team No AI N = 95 and Team AI N = 94, without specifying people, teams, or another unit. The odd count in a stated dyad arm is unexplained. Team headcounts, cluster counts, and observation counts remain null or unreported (PDF pp. 5-6).

Expert-rater count, rating aggregation, how a dyad solution contributes analysis rows, and the level of the reported SDs are not specified. The reconciled screening form leaves unit null for all outcomes; this extraction retains that uncertainty (PDF p. 5, Measures; PDF p. 6, Tables 2-3).

Table 3 does not give analyzed N, exact covariates, reference coding, coefficient/outcome standardization, or SE type/cluster adjustment. The symbol beta alone does not establish a standardized effect. Confirm these before standardizing or pooling the regression results (PDF p. 6).

Table 3 GenAI × Team rows are labelled interactions, while the Results prose describes the Quality row as the strongest team result. No direct team AI-versus-no-AI regression contrast or unambiguous reference group is printed; no simple effect has been calculated (PDF p. 6).
Table 6 H1–2 gives a team effect beta = 0.336, p < .001, with no identified model or contrast. Its relationship to Table 3 and the Results text is unresolved (PDF pp. 6, 8).

The no-AI protocol during the 45-minute AI training module is not described. The intervention combines AI access with the documented training, but a lack of corresponding control activity cannot be inferred (PDF p. 5, Procedures).
GPT-4 is named without a release year, exact model version, or data-collection date (PDF p. 5). The AI tool year is null.
No repository or analysis data are supplied. The Data availability statement offers data on reasonable request only (PDF p. 9). No author contact was made.

review_corrections.basis: 'conditions were assigned using a stratified randomization procedure accounting for prior AI exposure, job function, and digital fluency. This ensured a balanced representation across the four cells' (PDF p. 5, Procedures): the strata are traits of individual participants, so people were assigned to the four cells and dyads formed within the team cells. The paper does not describe the pairing step; flagged for Germán.
'The study recruited 371 mid-career professionals' (PDF p. 5, Procedures), all assigned to the four cells: the N column of Table 2 (PDF p. 6) sums to 371 (92 + 95 + 90 + 94).
